title: Hosted API lightning peak runbook — rapid-surge readiness
content:
Purpose:
Provide a concise, operationally-focused sheet for the "lightning" peak pattern — short (<10m) global token/QPS surges that require sub-minute mitigations and clear headroom targets. This is intentionally a tactical checklist + quick sizing reference rather than a full strategic capacity forecast.

TL;DR (operational numbers):
- Simulated single-minute global peak (P95 event): 1,200,000 tokens/sec total, ~18,000 QPS (avg tokens per request ~67).
- Minimum safe headroom target: 35% above simulated peak = 1,620,000 tokens/sec reserved globally.
- Target steady-state GPU utilization during normal peaks: 60–72% (to allow prewarm & burst absorb).
- Immediate reserve to hold in cold-start scenario (10s prewarm lag): 220,000 tokens/sec (distributed).

Assumptions used in quick calculations:
- Average request size during peak: 67 tokens (observed in past 6-month high-volume experiments).
- Model mix: 65% Llama-2-70B quantized variant, 25% Llama-2-13B, 10% small embedding/rerank endpoints.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (steady, with batching & KV caching): 32,000 tokens/sec on A100-equivalent; 18,000 tokens/sec on T4-like instances.
- Multi-region routing preserves locality: 60% of load in US, 25% EU, 15% APAC in the simulated window.

Quick regional sizing table (text sheet rows):
Region | sim_peak_tps | sim_peak_qps | headroom_pct | headroom_tps | suggested_gpu_equiv | notes
US   | 720,000 tokens/sec | 10,800 qps | 35% | 972,000 tokens/sec | 31 x A100-eq (est) | keep 3 hot spare slices
EU   | 300,000 tokens/sec | 4,480 qps | 35% | 405,000 tokens/sec | 13 x A100-eq (est) | prefer NVLink pools near eu-west-1
APAC | 180,000 tokens/sec | 2,720 qps | 35% | 243,000 tokens/sec | 8 x A100-eq (est) | enable cross-region fallback to US-west for non-SLA traffic
Global reserve summary: simulated peak 1,200,000 -> global headroom target 1,620,000 tokens/sec -> reserve delta = 420,000 tokens/sec. Reserve mapped to ~13 A100-eq spare GPUs globally for immediate absorb.

Operational controls & playbook (order matters):
1) Auto-prewarm (0–15s): ensure model slices flagged as "lightning-hot" in routing table. Action: infra oncall -> run prewarm command (route weight + prewarm API). Owner: Miguel R.
2) Ingress throttles (10–30s): apply per-customer token ceiling if runaway tenant observed. Default soft ceiling = 12 qps / 800 tokens/sec per key. Owner: Priya N.
3) Fast-fallback routing (30–90s): shift non-critical endpoints to smaller quantized model variants (L70B -> L13B quantized pipeline). Automated policy will move up to 20% of traffic. Owner: Runtime orchestrator (ops).
4) GPU slice expansion (60–180s): trigger ephemeral slice bring-up using reserved spare capacity. Ensure pool autoscaler has warm images available. Owner: SRE infra.
5) Post-event cooldown (5–30m): scale down reserved slices with staggered drain to avoid token storms. Owner: SRE infra + product.

Monitoring & alert thresholds (immediate):
- Token ingestion rate (global 1m avg) > 900k -> INFO alert to #infra-ops.
- Token ingestion rate (global 1m avg) > 1.2M -> P1 to oncall, start runbook.
- GPU pool utilization (regional 1m avg) > 78% -> P1 (risk of saturation).
- Prewarm success rate < 95% -> P2 (investigate cold images).
- Model fallback switch rate > 15% in 5m -> P2 (possible quality regression).

Quick-check spreadsheet formulas (for the sheet owner):
- headroom_tps = round(sim_peak_tps * (1 + headroom_pct))
- suggested_gpu_equiv = ceil(headroom_tps / effective_tokens_per_gpu)
- reserve_delta = headroom_tps_global - sim_peak_tps_global
(Where effective_tokens_per_gpu should be chosen per-region based on most common GPU family; note this is conservative and excludes spare for prewarm)

Risk notes:
- If model mix shifts to heavier L100B-class variants, effective_tokens_per_gpu can drop by 40–70% which invalidates this sheet; immediate re-eval required.
- Cross-region network throttles can introduce effective latency spikes that reduce batching efficiency; observed degradation: ~12% token/sec loss when RTT rises >120ms.

Open questions / items for follow-up:
- Confirm committed reserved GPUs for Q4 purchases (procurement ticket INF-1459).
- Validate runtime prewarm latency runbook with release-engineering; current images take median 6s cold boot but 95th percentile 22s.
- Should we apply a stricter headroom target for paid-SLA tenants? Proposal: +10% on top of base headroom.

Action items (next 7 days):
- [Ava] Run a 1-hour lightning-surge synthetic test (synthetic-surge-2026-08-05). Compare measured tokens/sec per GPU to assumptions.
- [Miguel] Harden prewarm API and publish checklist to Confluence.
- [Priya] Update weighted routing policy to include fast-fallback mapping and a telemetry tag for any automatic fallback switches.
- [Ethan] Create dashboard panel (global tokens/sec, regional headroom delta, prewarm success %) and add to incident playbook.

Notes for reviewers:
- This is a tactical sheet intended for oncall and infra planners. If approved, we will fold the core numbers into the canonical capacity model (confluence: peak-sim-2026) and schedule quarterly reviews.

Revision history:
- 2026-07-15 initial draft (Ava T.).
- 2026-07-20 added regional sizing and monitoring thresholds (Miguel R.).
- 2026-08-02 updated headroom to 35% after tabletop exercise (Ava T.).
